text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 3.2% today as oil prices dropped on growing hopes for a diplomatic resolution between the U.S. and Iran. The two countries held multi-hour talks at the UN on Wednesday, and reports that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz (a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments) if military pressure eases have eased market fears of a broader supply crisis. Oil fell for a fifth consecutive day on this optimism, undercutting the refining margins that drive profits for companies like this one.

The timing matters: the stock had surged from $410 to $424 in three days (September 15–18) when geopolitical tensions were at their peak and oil looked scarce. Now that a diplomatic path seems possible, that supply-crisis premium has unwound. Refineries are running at a high 96.8% capacity, so the upside from constrained supply is fading.
